study: Isolated six-world PySR identifiability: exact versus velocity-difference acceleration
scientific_question: With identical informative trajectories, distinguish backend search limits, derivative-label error and candidate packaging limits before any new Agent benchmark.

data.weighting: Equal total weight per trajectory; equal weight per interior sample within trajectory.
data.design: The same registered position, velocity, property and launch-time controls for every world; several quadrants/radii, independent mass/charge controls, repeated complete initial states at launch times 3,7,11,17,23,29,31.
data.holdout: Eight separately specified new initial states, launch times and properties; never used for search, parameter fitting, coefficient-sharing acceptance or candidate selection.
data.exact_labels: Vendor acceleration evaluated only by the isolated dataset generator at each observed interior state; stored in a separate diagnostic-only side table, never in production probe records.

arms.A_exact: Direct PySR on common interior states and exact acceleration labels.
arms.B_velocity_difference: The identical direct backend runner on the same states and weights, with prepare_dataset velocity-difference targets as the only changed search input. Neither arm uses generic linear seeds. This is not a third production-tool search.

search.axis_allocation: The same fixed 30-second PySR timeout for each of the two axes in both arms; actual per-axis and total timings recorded, including any soft-timeout overrun.
search.parent_hard_timeout: Parent stops an owned worker about 63 seconds after its search phase begins (60 seconds requested search plus 3 seconds of timeout/result-transport tolerance). This is an offline diagnostic, not a claim of strict 60-second execution.
search.postprocessing: The identical production selector/exporter is applied after each direct search with a separate 10-second allowance. Only arm-specific discovery targets enter this step; independent holdout is never used. Search and postprocessing times are reported separately.
search.warmup: Synthetic-only compilation in each isolated process, measured separately from search; no contest world or archive data.

reporting: Raw PySR equations, loss and complexity frontier, selected strictly by training loss/complexity.
All equations scored on fixed holdout after search, with no best-of-holdout answer selection.
Acceleration NRMSE = sqrt(weighted squared error / weighted exact acceleration squared), per axis and energy-weighted combined vector.
Actual derivative-label error on common train and holdout states.
Exported coefficient count and compatibility with the existing five-parameter law limit.
Single-axis delivery and final packaged candidate results reported separately from raw backend results.
Warmup, actual per-axis/search, post-search diagnostic evaluation and total wall time; partial results/errors retained.
Dataset and scientific-source SHA256 recorded before execution.
limitations: This is an informative-data offline diagnostic, not a contest score or an autonomous Agent result. A single stochastic multithreaded run cannot prove search impossibility; no repeated seeds, hand-supplied formulas or per-world operator tuning are allowed in this registered batch. Initial radii 1.5-4 provide limited identification of a 0.05 softening scale: epsilon squared / r squared is only about 1.6e-4 to 1.1e-3. Low heldout NRMSE establishes domain prediction accuracy, not recovery of every small term or an exact symbolic identity.
